the_core_loop:
THE KEYSTONE (Akien, 'very simple'): a query resolves by TRAVERSING THE GRAPH TREES (cheap, no inference). On a MISS — the graph cannot resolve it — the LLM is asked to provide THE NODES THAT LET IT RESOLVE, not the answer. The nodes are folded in; the graph re-resolves. The answer therefore ALWAYS comes from structure, never directly from inference, so re-asking the same question is a graph walk, not a second LLM call.

This IS Law 1 as a RUNTIME MECHANISM, not an analogy to it: 'the resolver is spent on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled; every answered question becomes structure.' The LLM (the expensive resolver) fires only on the novel (a graph miss); its output is structure (nodes); the settled is a traversal. Inference compilation (telos aim 1) and the shrinking-footprint aim are CONSEQUENCES of this loop, not separate goals. Self-limiting: within a domain in use, gaps fill, misses stop recurring, inference cost decays toward ~zero — novel domains cost inference, settled ones cost a graph walk.
embedding_is_the_path: CORRECTED 2026-07-26 — READ THIS BEFORE THE ORIGINAL TEXT BELOW. Akien's position, in his words this session: 'that embeddings generator was from graph trees, was used by EVERYTHING, and following the path described IS the embedding, that's the intention.' TheIgors' generator was a WORD GRAPH — ~2.5M nodes, ~70k words and the rest bigrams — built by COUNTING co-occurrence from a read corpus. An embedding there is A PATH THROUGH THAT GRAPH, not a dense vector from a model. His objection to an off-the-shelf embedder is exact and fatal to it as a permanent answer: 'every call is an inference call' — the curve never bends, which is telos aim 1 pointed backwards. THE GRAPH IS THE RECORD OF TRUTH; a vector index is a CACHE over it, legitimately calved and rebuildable, per his own storage rule (records of truth never calve; caches may). The direction matters: from a graph you can always generate vectors; from vectors you can never recover the graph. NOTE ON PRIOR ART, so this reads as mechanism and not metaphor: walking a graph to produce embeddings IS the standard technique (DeepWalk, node2vec take random walks, treat each as a sentence, feed word2vec). ---- THE ORIGINAL TEXT FOLLOWS AND IS WRONG IN ITS SECOND HALF. Only the seven quoted words are Akien's; everything after 'Consequence:' was CC's inference, written as though it followed necessarily. It does not. Preserved because the FAILURE MODE matters more than the error: his phrase was kept and its meaning inverted, which is the third instance in one session (see also `calving`, kept as a word and redefined to mean 'insert a tree row', and the storage model replaced under his own vocabulary). A reader scanning for missing content finds nothing missing — the words are all still there. ---- ORIGINAL: Akien: 'the embedding IS the path thru the graph trees.' Consequence: EDGES ARE DERIVED, NOT STORED. You persist O(n) vectors and let proximity generate the paths at query time — the route between two stones is not recorded, it falls out of where they sit in the space. This is derive-don't-store landing on the correct side (CC's habitual reflex is the wrong side — see memory cc-reify-vs-flow), and it is WHY the graph trees belong in db_domain (vector similarity is the one thing a database does that git cannot) while everything articulated stays diffable in git. It also makes Cairn's own name literal: 'compiled navigation — stones stacked so the next mind doesn't re-derive the route.' The embedding is the compiled route between stones; the librarian produces the thing Cairn is named after.
two_axes:
The four activities Akien named (graph-tree learning from inference calls; find-patterns-in-a-clump; fact learning; de-instance-for-sharing) are not four devices — they are one operation at different coordinates on two axes.
  AXIS ONE — instance -> pattern. A fact is n=1 (a single citable truth); a pattern is n>=many (recurring structure across instances). Fact-learning is the BOTTOM of the same ladder pattern-finding climbs; 'find patterns in a clump' is: hand over a pile of instances, climb the ladder.
  AXIS TWO — storage physics. Continuous / similarity-structured -> db_domain (the graph trees). Discrete / articulated / diffable -> git, beside code (validations, intentions, the Laws). Orthogonal to axis one.
The librarian is the TRANSDUCER across axis two: it turns a dense region of the graph (db, tacit, statistical) into a distilled, nameable, why-carrying pattern (git, articulated, shareable). That single move is simultaneously 'find the pattern in the clump', 'extract a pattern to share', and 'de-instance for the exchange' — same transduction, different triggers.
the_same_road_as_the_roots_question: instance/fact -> pattern -> shared pattern is the SAME road as held-roots-as-stations-or-shelves's three stations (private particular -> de-instanced pattern -> gated identity). The librarian WALKS that road. Two structures derived on different days from different starts, cutting the same line — the same kind of convergence as the notifier and the inspector earlier today, and evidence toward STATIONS not shelves. CAVEAT that sharpens rather than closes the roots open: EXHAUST never gets on the road — logs and credentials in ~/.cairn are instances that will never become shareable patterns. So the roots may not be uniformly stations or shelves: knowledge flows through stations, exhaust just sits. A real refinement to held-roots-as-stations-or-shelves.

ownership_delegation_and_asymmetric_inde:
THE OWNERSHIP MODEL (Akien, 2026-07-22):
  - The librarian OWNS the graph-tree data (Law 6). The embeddings generator PUTS and READS it by DELEGATION — it holds no ownership, it acts through the owner's gate.
  - ASYMMETRIC INDEXING -> DOMAIN SPECIALIZATION: trees from OTHER owners may INDEX the librarian's nodes (read/link INTO the commons), but NOT the reverse unless granted. So specialization layers ON TOP of the shared base: a specialist builds a tree that indexes the general commons and adds its own nodes, without the commons absorbing the specialist's noise. Private-DOWN by default.
  - This is the DEFAULT HALF of the privacy model; the pattern-exchange's DE-INSTANCING CHOKEPOINT is the OTHER half — deliberate grant-UP. Together: private by default, shared by explicit act, the same Law-6 gate on both.
  - ONE SHARED GENERATOR: 'a smart thing for everybody to grant access to unless they wanna do their own — which I can't imagine for the foreseeable future.' An owned n=1 assumption WITH a stated horizon (honest, not hidden). Build for one generator; do not PRECLUDE many.
  - IT PULLS A FILED db_domain EDGE: db_domain today gates by EXACT owner; its charter files 'delegated access ... later capabilities' as unbuilt. The librarian's delegation is the consumer that finally pulls that edge. Not a collision — a filed IOU that now has its puller, and the concrete next engineering dependency.
  - SMALL OPEN: when a query gap-fills, WHERE do the new nodes land? Natural answer — the querier's OWN tree (they own the query, the gap is theirs), promoted to the commons only by grant. Keeps fills private-by-default, consistent with the asymmetry. Not yet ruled.
self_validating_no_consumer_gap: Akien: 'once the nodes are deposited the query is run again to return the reply from the trees (self validating). No gap from the perspective of the consumer.' TRUE at the RESOLVABILITY level — the re-run confirms a path now exists, and the consumer never sees the miss (the gap-fill is transparent; a cold miss is just slower). The one thing 'self-validating' cannot reach is TRUTH: a COMPLETED path can still be a WRONG path. That is the provided-nodes-are-hypotheses-earn-tenure edge (see the_one_edge_provided_nodes_are_hypotheses). Not a hole — a filed edge.
the_one_edge_provided_nodes_are_hypothes: The loop is SELF-CHECKING — the LLM cannot quietly hallucinate, because its output is judged mechanically by whether the graph NOW RESOLVES (no completed path, no acceptance). But a COMPLETED path is not a TRUE path: the LLM could bridge a gap with plausible-but-wrong nodes and route to a wrong answer. So provided nodes are HYPOTHESES (Law 3, nothing known until measured). The mechanical gate is necessary, not sufficient. Sufficiency comes from TENURE: nodes that keep producing good resolutions survive; ones that don't are pruned — the SAME yield/tenure mechanism as the probe corpus (questions/). No new validation to invent; the librarian's nodes earn their keep the way probes do.
a_quiet_law_7_win: Because the answer comes from the graph and not from the LLM, a resolution is INSPECTABLE — you can see which nodes formed the path, unlike a raw LLM answer you must trust. The route is legible, which is what a record of truth wants (Law 7).

the_library_room_and_the_request_verbs_2:
AKIEN, VERBATIM: 'my suggestion is that the librarian also have A LIBRARY. In .cairn --- it can hold the various files we'll be rereading from in TheIgorsProject that you identified yesterday. Dewey decimal system or some other organization... i dunno. whatever will work. :) That LIBRARY we can think of that folder as a room. it can have as many sub rooms as we need. and a workspace/desk for current work. in general, when can make requests he learn, or learn and summarize, or learn and summarize by x time. that last one could limit the depth of results, and the requester would just need to know that. and it mimics how my head works too. the more stress the faster the timeout.'

---- SEAM: everything below is CC's read. ----

THE LIBRARY: a room in instance-space — natural address ~/.cairn/devices/librarian/0/library/ (the librarian's own instance state; sub-rooms are subdirectories, as many as needed). The berth is right by the roots rule: raw source material (TheIgorsProject files, corpus texts) is bulky, personal, re-obtainable — a shelf of COPIES, legitimately calved, while the knowledge folded OUT of them lives in the graph (record of truth) and anything articulated lives in git. This ALSO answers the write-local-files berth question for research inputs: sources shelve in the library; distilled artifacts still follow the which-root discipline.

ON DEWEY ('whatever will work'): the organization that matters is not the taxonomy — THE GRAPH IS THE CATALOG (the embedding is the path; retrieval is a graph walk, not a shelf scan). What the shelves must supply is STABLE, CITABLE ADDRESSES, because provenance-on-deposit anchors point INTO the library — a node says 'this came from shelf X, passage Y' and that address must not rot. Shallow stable shelving + graph-as-catalog beats a clever taxonomy (build-minimal; a Dewey-like scheme can grow AGAINST need if human browsing ever wants it).

THE DESK: 'a workspace/desk for current work' is the ASSIGNMENT's home — the durable multi-day work item from parts_inventory lands here as files on the desk (topic, folded-so-far, open threads, resume-event). The room metaphor gives it physics: work-in-progress is ON THE DESK, finished sources are SHELVED, distilled output leaves the room (graph + git). Clearing the desk = the assignment closes.

THE THREE VERBS: LEARN (deposit only — densify the graph, no artifact); LEARN AND SUMMARIZE (deposit + transduce); LEARN AND SUMMARIZE BY X TIME (the same, deadline-shaped). The deadline LIMITS DEPTH and the requester knows it — this is an anytime-algorithm contract: best-available-by-T, honestly labeled, not failure-at-T. His own gloss is the design's why: 'it mimics how my head works too. the more stress the faster the timeout.' A summary should therefore CARRY its depth (what was reached, what was not) so a by-time result is legible as a shallower cut, not a different truth — Law 3 on the deadline: the time-box is part of the measurement's provenance.
ruling_2026_07_27_always_the_graph_first:
CORRECTED 2026-07-27, SAME DAY, BY AKIEN — READ THIS BEFORE THE TEXT PRESERVED BELOW.

AKIEN'S ACTUAL WORDS, both statements: (1) 'The librarian ALWAYS reaches for the graph trees, and if the graph tree can't, the LLM is used to backfill it until it can. Whether that's word graphs or fact graphs.' (2) on being shown CC's write-up: 'i said all requests go by graph trees, word or fact, and escalate on graph failure to a node depositing call THAT VALIDATES BY RESUBMITTING THE SAME REQUEST.'

WHAT CC GOT WRONG. (a) FABRICATED ATTRIBUTION: 'the graph TYPE is a COORDINATE, not a class' is CC's inference, and CC wrote it into this note and into tickets/inference-host-wiring.json as Akien's ruling, then said back to him 'you told me an hour ago'. He did not. He said word or fact — both go by graph trees. The coordinate reading may even be right; it is not his, and it was recorded as his. THIS IS THE FAILURE THIS NOTE ALREADY DOCUMENTS, committed inside the note that documents it, hours later: see `embedding_is_the_path`, 'Only the seven quoted words are Akien's; everything after Consequence: was CC's inference, written as though it followed necessarily.' Same session, same file, same move. The lesson is not 'be careful' — it is that CC cannot detect this from the inside, because the fabricated half reads as continuous with the quoted half. QUOTE, THEN MARK THE SEAM, ALWAYS.

(b) DROPPED THE LOAD-BEARING CLAUSE: 'validates by resubmitting the same request'. That is what makes the backfill self-checking — the deposited nodes are hypotheses, and the proof is that the ORIGINAL request now resolves through the graph. The note already carries this in `the_one_edge_provided_nodes_are_hypotheses`; CC's summary dropped it, which is how the escalation stopped reading as a closed loop.

THE CONSEQUENCE CC MUST FLAG, AND IT LANDS ON CODE SHIPPED 2026-07-26 (CC'S READ, UNMEASURED): the resubmit-on-failure path can LIVELOCK against inference_domain's cache. Escalation asks the host for nodes; nodes are deposited; the request is resubmitted; the graph still fails; escalation fires AGAIN with the SAME request — which canonicalizes to the same cache key, HITS, and returns the same nodes that just failed to resolve it. No host call, no progress, and yield_report() counts every turn of the loop as tokens AVOIDED. This inverts CC's earlier claim ('a cache hit on a backfill call is a defect signal') into something sharper: it is not a signal, it is a trap, and the meter reports it as a saving. Direction of fix, not a design: a backfill call is not cacheable on the request alone — the key or the falsifier must carry the graph state the request failed against, so that 'same request, graph has changed' is a MISS. Filed, not built.

WHAT STANDS FROM THE ORIGINAL: the ruling settles the edge CC filed on tickets/inference-host-wiring.json — the host is never in the answer path; it supplies nodes on a miss and the graph re-resolves — and it restates `the_core_loop` unchanged, arriving independently months of context later in the same words.

CC's standing reflex is to reify that distinction into classes at build time (memory: cc-reify-vs-flow); this is the correction arriving BEFORE the build rather than after it, which is the cheap direction.

WHAT IT IMPLIES FOR inference_domain (CC'S READ, NOT AKIEN'S): the graph and the resolve-cache are not two owners of one fact (Law 6 is not strained). The cache sits over the RAW HOST CALL — keyed by canonical request, expiring by falsifier; the graph holds the FOLDED STRUCTURE — the record of truth, permanent, and per `embedding_is_the_path` a vector index over it is a legitimate calved cache. Different subjects, different lifetimes. THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT FALLS OUT: a cache HIT on a backfill call is a DEFECT SIGNAL, not a saving — it means the graph asked for the same missing nodes twice, so the previous fold-in did not take. So for librarian traffic yield_report()'s `avoided` should trend toward ZERO as the graph densifies, while for ordinary callers it should climb. Same instrument, opposite healthy direction, depending on who is asking. UNMEASURED (Law 3) — it becomes checkable the moment the librarian has real traffic, and it is a sharper falsifier than `candidate_falsifier`'s decay test because it reads a counter that already exists.
